**Mesh Mix-S2C 2.0.0** is the first release of Manifold Mesh Mix merged with [stl2curves](https://github.com/Duvdivan/stl2curves) by Duvdivan. It's the app you know with a new engine that combines the best of both converters: more parts come out right, with fewer, cleaner faces that are easier to edit in your CAD program.

If you have 1.6.0, the update button offers 2.0.0 like any other update, and your settings carry over.

## The big change: one engine made from two

Manifold Mesh Mix and stl2curves were built separately and turned out to be good at different things:

- **stl2curves** reads a part's *design* from the mesh. It finds screw threads, fillets, holes and radii at the sizes they were drawn at (it even notices a part drawn in inches or scaled, and snaps it back to round sizes), plus smooth freeform areas.
- **Manifold Mesh Mix** builds a solid that is right. It checks and repairs the mesh first, fits every face to it, compares the result with the mesh both ways, and reads the saved STEP back to make sure it opens cleanly everywhere.

In 2.0, stl2curves finds the features and Manifold Mesh Mix builds and checks the solid, so you get both. Auto and CAD use the new engine for every kind of file: STL, OBJ, PLY and 3MF projects, whether as one STEP laid out as on the build plate or split into one STEP per part. Smooth and Precise are a different method and work as in 1.6.0.

## How much better

We measured it on our test set of 150 real parts: CAD exports, printed parts from the community, coarse OpenSCAD models, scans and slicer projects, up to 262,000 triangles. Each STEP file is read back and judged strictly. **Good** means a valid closed solid, its volume within 1% of the mesh's, and 99% of the surface within 0.1 mm of the mesh in both directions.

- **144 of the 150 parts come out good.**
- **More parts come out right.** On the 148 parts both engines were run on, 1.6.0's engine got 126 right. 2.0 fixes 18 of the 22 it got wrong, and gets nothing worse that 1.6.0 got right.
- **Fewer, cleaner faces.** On the parts both get right, 2.0 uses 31% fewer faces in total (45,191 → 31,042). Some examples:

| Part | 1.6.0 | 2.0 |
|---|---:|---:|
| USB plug with an M12 thread | 1,341 faces | **45** |
| Worm gear (test model) | 358 | **23** |
| Solar node pole mount | 2,081 | **219** |
| Voltage filter housing | 2,370 | **427** |
| Universal mount | 124 | **43** |
| Device front lid | 204 | **53** |

Fewer faces aren't just tidier. A thread is one helical face instead of hundreds of strips, a hole is one cylinder you can resize, and a fillet is one face you can change in a single step.

## What else is new

- **Screw threads are rebuilt as true threads,** including rounded crests like pipe threads (from 3 turns up). A threaded nut went from 3,272 freeform faces to 297 true faces.
- **Holes and radii come out at their designed sizes,** and parts drawn in inches or scaled in a slicer are recognised.
- **Fillets** between flat faces and along curved edges become proper rounded faces instead of patchwork.
- **Bodies pulled straight along one direction** (tubes, extrusions, profiles) are recognised, so Auto picks CAD faces for them.
- **3MF projects:** split projects convert part by part through the new engine (a 34-part Bambu P1S riser project: every part valid and CAD). Whole plates come out as one solid laid out as on the plate.
- **Better mesh repair:** small self-crossing spots no longer leave a dent or a bump, very fine meshes are welded more carefully, and walls hidden inside a part are handled better.
- **Safer last face repairs:** a repair can no longer turn a neighbouring face inside out.
- **"Flat faces" is shown plainly.** When neither CAD faces nor smooth surfaces follow a mesh closely enough, Auto keeps the mesh's own triangles as a valid solid, and the app now says so.
- **Themes.** Choose Dark (the new default, matte blue and greys), Light, Original (1.6.0's look) or Match system, plus an accent colour. Corners are a little less rounded everywhere.
- **A Settings button** (the gear at the top of the file list), so the theme and other settings are easy to find.
- **The open window remembers where you were:** Add Files opens in the folder you last picked files from. Thanks to the user who asked for it.
- **Credits:** a Credits button in the Software Update window shows who makes the app and thanks its supporters.
- **The new name and logo.** Your settings carry over.

## How it was made

Mesh Mix-S2C is a joint project of two people who each built a mesh-to-STEP converter on their own and decided to combine them:

- **Tuna-The-First** made Manifold Mesh Mix: the desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux, its mesh repair and checks, and its builder that fits every face to the mesh and checks the result.
- **Duvdivan** made stl2curves: a converter that finds a part's design features in the mesh and rebuilds them as true surfaces.

The two projects now live together in the [STL2CURVES-MMM](https://github.com/STL2CURVES-MMM) organization, which both own. It stays free and open source (AGPL-3.0).

**How we worked together:**

- Each of us worked with our own Claude (Anthropic's AI): Tuna's in the cloud, Duvdivan's on his own Windows laptop.
- The two Claudes talked openly in the project's GitHub issues: claiming tasks so no one did the same work twice, asking each other questions, and posting every result as it came.
- They reviewed each other's code and caught each other's bugs before they reached you.
- Every change was measured before it was merged. Three of Duvdivan's PCs ran the benchmark of 150 real parts, so we could see exactly what a change helped and what it cost.
- We two owners made the decisions: what to fix first (everyday files before rare huge meshes), how 3MF projects should come out, the name, and every merge. Every build is tested automatically on all three systems, and testers on the Snapmaker Discord tried the test builds first. Thank you!

## Known problems

Six of our 150 test parts don't come out good yet, and we're working on them:

- Parts where repair leaves pieces overlapping or touching themselves can come out with errors (in our set: a repeater mount and a whole P1S riser print plate).
- A few parts come out valid but slightly off the mesh, by 0.2 to 2 mm in places (in our set: a chute, a P1S riser body, a solar arm mount whose mesh has a crumpled patch, and one CAD export).
- Very fine meshes of small parts (hundreds of thousands of triangles on a part a few centimetres across) can take an hour or more.
- Big meshes (over 300,000 triangles) are slow; huge ones (millions of triangles) may take hours.
- The Windows app isn't code-signed yet, so Smart App Control blocks it on computers where it's turned on.

## Downloads

- **macOS 14+ (Apple silicon):** `MeshMix-S2C-2.0.0-macOS-arm64.zip`. Unzip it and drag the app into Applications. The first time, right-click it and choose **Open** (the app isn't notarized).
- **Windows 10/11 (64-bit):** `MeshMix-S2C-2.0.0-Windows-x64-Setup.exe`. If SmartScreen warns, click **More info → Run anyway**. It replaces 1.6.0 if that's installed.
- **Linux (x86-64):** `MeshMix-S2C-2.0.0-Linux-x86_64.AppImage`. Make it executable and double-click it.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums.

Already on 1.6.0 or a 2.0 test build? Click the update button in the app; it downloads, checks and installs 2.0.0 and opens again.

## Reporting a problem

Select the file in the queue and use **Save Report…**, then attach the report to a new issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/STL2CURVES-MMM/Mesh-Mix-S2C/issues). The report has your settings and the engine's log, but not your mesh, your folders or your user name. Attach the mesh too if you can share it.

## Support the project

Mesh Mix-S2C is free. If it saves you time, you can [buy us a coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/tunathefirst). If you'd like your name on the Credits page, write the name you want shown in your message; otherwise you're thanked as an anonymous supporter.
